Yes, Chinese has a tonal system where small pronunciation errors can completely change meanings, and speaking too early may reinforce incorrect tonal patterns that are hard to fix.
No, Kay's primary goal is to read literature and academic papers in Chinese, not to use it in real-life conversation.
It is not especially undesirable for Kay right now, since spoken communication is only a secondary concern and they do not expect to need it for several years.
